Expanded Blood Feats

Many question the existence of sanguimancy and haemothurgy as separate magical traditions. Blood is blood, is it not? An understandable question, if one that will get dismissive eye rolls from practitioners of both traditions. Why are sprinting and distance running separate sports? After all, running is running, is it not? As that example proves, often the difference comes down to specifics.

Sanguimancy is a broader tradition, available to more people. You can learn sanguimancy at any time during your studies, and you don’t even need to know other magic. It’s also a safer tradition, building a pool of power that you draw from. Once that pool is empty, your access to sanguimancy goes away until you rebuild it.

On the other hand, haemothurgy is a tradition of blood magic deeply tied with the process of magic. Those without the talent and inclination for magic find it much more difficult to pick up. It’s also far more reckless, pulling directly from the lifeblood of the user instead of building a buffer. It’s possible for a reckless or careless haemothurge to meet their end at the hands of their own magic.

Given how interrelated haemothurgy and sanguimancy are, it only makes sense that there is overlap between the two. Below are feats that deal with this overlap, as well as a new sanguimancer feat.

New Magic Item Types.name: New Magic Item Types
New Magic Item Types.text:
Existing Rings as Power Rings

There are many ring items in the core game, like the Ring of Wizardry or the Ring of Swimming. You can choose to give these rings the abilities of power rings, like a specific magic weapon has the power of a striking rune. To do so, look at the level of the specific magic ring and round it down to the nearest power ring. For example, a Ring of Lies is a level 10 item, so it would have the properties of an iron power ring, while a Ring of Climbing, a level 12 item, would have the power of a silver power ring. If the item gives you an item bonus to a skill, remove that bonus. Be aware that this rule will increase the power of ring items significantly, should you choose to implement it.

Unlimited Power

Power Rings are designed to be able to fit into any existing game without further changes being required; however, some GMs may feel they would prefer that the bonuses of a power ring always be active. If you are among these GMs, you can change the power rings so that their item bonus to spell attack rolls are always active; if you do so, simply apply the item bonus to any spell attack rolls of the wearer and add the following text to the end of the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Gb7SeieEvd0pL2Eh]{Sure Strike} spell: “The sure strike spell does not apply to spell attack rolls.”

Power Rings

Power rings represent the methods by which spellcasters hone their attack spells into more formiddable threats, albeit, usually with their most consistent forms of magic: cantrips.

Scepters

Magic users and artificers are constantly working to advance the art and science of casting of spells and improve the magic items that might aid them. One way that has resurfaced in popularity is to use magic scepters that feed off the users current magic abilities to enhance and alter the magic they are casting. Scepters come in many materials and shapes, though most of them have a cylindrical base that is easy to hold on in one hand. They are often decorated and embellished in a way that belies their purpose. Using a scepter requires holding it in one hand. Scepters always grant access to spellshape and a once per day activated effect. activated effects will require sacrificing a spell slot of a rank indicated by the effect. If you are a prepared spellcaster, you choose one of your prepared spells to lose as if you had cast it. Spontaneous casters use one of their daily spell slots as if they had cast a spell from it. Most scepters will have a minimum and/or maximum spell slot rank required to activate it, listed in the effect.

Scepters have a limited capacity to convert spells into actuated effects, but similar to wands they can be overloaded to allow for additional uses. If you have already used the actuated effect of a scepter, you can attempt to Overload it. Roll a DC 10 flat check. On a success the activation happens as normal, but the scepter gains the broken condition and cannot be used for either the Spellshape or actuated effect. On a failure, the effect does not happen, you lose the actions, and the scepter gains the broken condition. In either case, the scepter cannot be repaired until the next time you make your daily preparations. Repairing a scepter requires using the Repair action or sacrificing a daily spell slot of the minimum rank required to activate the scepter.

Dynamic Spell Sage.name: Dynamic Spell Sage
Dynamic Spell Sage.text:
Alternate Rule: Universal Dynamism

For some groups, the power and flexibility of spellcasters might feel a bit lacking. If that’s the case for your group, you might consider allowing spellcasters to cast the dynamic versions of all of the spells listed without the dynamic spellsage archetype. You can then apply all of the spell adjustments from the dynamic mastery section. Like the free archetype variant rule from the GM Core, this variant increases a character’s versatility without any associated cost (though this variant is less impactful than free archetype).

Applying universal dynamism requires adjusting the dynamic spellsage archetype. Replace the benefits of the Dynamic Spellsage Dedication with your choice of the Cantrip Expansion or Familiar class feats.

uncommon

Dynamic spellsages are experts of magical manipulation. Instead of delving into the more typical path of the study of spellshapes, they focus primarily on bringing out the full potential of spells that can already be cast in multiple different ways. Through their spellcraft, magic can be compressed into a fraction of its normal power, or expanded to henceforth unknown levels. Most scholars of magical history believe that at least some of the flexible spells that are in frequent use today, such as heal or force barrage, were developed by the tinkering of dynamic spellsages in ages past.

Dynamic Mastery

As a dynamic spellsage, you’ve mastered a collection of variable action spells, allowing you to Cast them to greater effect. Whenever you can choose a dynamic mastery spell, select from the following list. These spells are sorted by source and type. Each mastery allows you to modify one of the options for casting the spell. The benefits do not apply to any of the other action costs.

Whenever you gain dynamic mastery in additional spells, you can also immediately retrain all of your existing dynamic mastery selections.

Core Variable Action Spells

These variable action spells appear in Pathfinder Player Core or Pathfinder Player Core 2. Apply the following enhancements to the spells that you select for your dynamic mastery.

If you do, each missile deals 1d8+1 damage instead of 1d4+1.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.wdA52JJnsuQWeyqz]{Harm}: When you cast the 3-action version of the spell, you can choose any radius up to 40 feet.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal}: When you cast the 3-action version of the spell, you can choose any radius up to 40 feet.

Expanded Core Spells

These existing Pathfinder spells have new variable action versions in this book which are listed in the Dynamic Spell Variants section. These dynamic versions typically trade some of the range or duration of the pre-existing spell for the versatility of being able to cast 1- action, 2-action, and 3-action versions.

When you select one of these expanded core spells for dynamic mastery, however, you can regain the full strength of the default spell version while also retaining the dynamic spellcasting options. For all of these spells except @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.items.HpZlCkpwAsStILMl]{Dynamic Guidance} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.items.u8BuGKcF9VYk9TZi]{Dynamic Shield}, replace the 2-action version with the 2-action spell that shares its name without the word dynamic. For example, replace the 2-action version of dynamic fireball with the standard fireball spell. For dynamic guidance and dynamic shield, instead replace the 1-action version of the dynamic spell with its standard version.

These spells are entirely new to this book. If you select one of these spells for your dynamic mastery, apply the following adjustments.

Boom-A-Rang: When you cast the 2-action version of the spell, increase the slashing damage by 1d8.

Crushing Stampede: When you cast the 2-action version of the spell, you can select any radius between 20 feet and 40 feet.

Spirit Boundary: When you cast the 2-action version of the spell, you can select any radius between 5 feet and 30 feet.

Targeted Ward: When you cast the 2-action version of the spell, increase the range to 60 feet.

Elemental Aspects.name: Elemental Aspects
Elemental Aspects.text:
All elemental aspects have the following statistics in addition to the statistics listed for their aspect.

Traits elemental

Senses darkvision

Skills Lore in its associated element

Save Adjustments Choose a save for each modifier: –2,+0,+1

Heightened (8th) The aspect gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.u098thIGDlrHC8G8]{Caster} aspect ability along with the Elemental Magic spells listed for the aspect. Cantrip: see aspect, 1st: see aspect, 2nd: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Fr58LDSrbndgld9n]{Resist Energy}, 3rd: see aspect, 4th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.aqRYNoSvxsVfqglH]{Unfettered Movement}, 5th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.fg5ZlSVXzGHNJfbO]{Elemental Breath} (elemental trait only), 6th: see aspect, 7th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.m2xFMNyQiUKQDRaj]{Energy Aegis}, 8th: see aspect

Air Aspect

This elemental rages with whistling winds, like a zephyr hawk or a picture-in-cloud.

Traits air

Languages Sussuran

Skills Acrobatics, Athletics

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.6UOfXUjzQQrz03Y9]{Sourced} (rain clouds or blustering winds)

Windy Aura (air, aura 15 feet) Winds whip around the aspect making it hard to approach. Ranged attacks against creatures within the area take a –1 circumstance penalty and the area is difficult terrain to creatures in flight.

Speed 15 feet, fly 30 feet

Ranged 1 primary (range 30 feet), Damage 1d6 + rank bludgeoning or 1d4 + rank electricity

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains the Storm Aura ability.

Storm Aura Creatures within the aspect’s Windy Aura are also concealed, and all creatures outside the aura become concealed to creatures within it. The aspect is immune to the concealed condition from this ability.

Heightened (8th) Elemental Magic Cantrip: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.dDiOnjcsBFbAvP6t]{Gale Blast}; 1st: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.KcLVELhCUcKXxiKE]{Tailwind}; 3rd: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.it4ZsAi6XgvGcodc]{Wall of Wind}; 6th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.TDNlDWbYb58Y55Da]{Chain Lightning}, 8th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.wi405lBjPcbF1DeR]{Punishing Winds}

Earth Aspect

This dragon is empowered by otherworldly forces, like diabolic dragons or brine dragons.

Traits earth

Senses tremorsense (15 feet) imprecise

Languages Petran

Skills Athletics, Survival

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.6UOfXUjzQQrz03Y9]{Sourced} (boulder)

Rocky Aura (aura 15 feet, earth) The earth hardens and sharpens around the aspect. When the aspect gains actions for the turn, it creates difficult terrain within the area that lasts until the beginning of your next turn. The aspect treats this difficult terrain as normal terrain.

Speed 20 feet

Melee 1 slam Damage 1d8 + rank bludgeoning

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains the Aftershock activity.

Aftershock 2 (earth) Frequency once per minute; Effect The aspect deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage per rank of the spell to all creatures within 15 feet with a basic Reflex save. Creatures that critically fail their save are knocked prone.

Heightened (8th) Elemental Magic Cantrip: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.zA0jNIBRgLsyTpbm]{Scatter Scree}; 1st: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Rn2LkoSq1XhLsODV]{Pummeling Rubble}; 3rd: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.gPvtmKMRpg9I9D7H]{Earthbind}; 6th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.znv4ECL7ZtuiagtA]{Petrify}, 8th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.x7SPrsRxGb2Vy2nu]{Earthquake}

Fire Aspect

This burning hot elemental is made of flame, like a cinder rat or living magma.

Traits fire

Languages Pyric

Skills Acrobatics, Intimidation

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.6UOfXUjzQQrz03Y9]{Sourced} (fire)

Resistances cold and fire; Weaknesses water

Heat Aura (aura 15 feet, fire) The aspect gives off intense heat. It sheds bright light in the area, and dim light 15 feet beyond that. Creatures that end their turn within the bright light take fire damage equal to twice the rank of the spell with a basic Fortitude save. The aspect can spend a single action with the concentrate trait to suppress or resume the damage from this aura. The aspect is immune to its own heat aura.

Speed 25 feet

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.rU0OMGjiOo6xc7BR]{Flier} The aspect has the Flier aspect ability.

Melee 1 primary Damage 1d6 + rank fire or Ranged 1 primary (range 30 feet), Damage 1d4 + rank fire

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains immunity to fire and creatures that fail their save against its Heat Aura take persistent fire damage equal to the rank of the spell or twice the rank of the spell if they critically fail their save. Flammable objects in the area can also catch fire (subject to GM discretion).

Heightened (8th) Elemental Magic cantrip: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.6DfLZBl8wKIV03Iq]{Ignition}, 1st: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.y6rAdMK6EFlV6U0t]{Breathe Fire}; 3rd: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.sxQZ6yqTn0czJxVd]{Fireball}; 6th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Gn5deIoobHpd3SiR]{Flame Vortex}, 8th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.fBoiPXmcIO50OFFR]{Boil Blood}

Metal Aspect

This steely elemental is made of sharp metals, like a rust scarab or oregorger.

Traits metal

Languages Talican

Skills Athletics, Crafting

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.6UOfXUjzQQrz03Y9]{Sourced} (metal objects)

Resistances electricity; Weaknesses fire

Magnetism Aura (aura 15 feet, metal) Metals are interfered with within the aspect’s aura. Strikes made with metal weapons have a –1 circumstance penalty within the area.

Speed 25 feet

Melee 1 primary, Damage 1d8 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing Ranged 1 secondary (range 60 feet), Damage 1d6 + rank piercing or slashing

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains the Repulsion activity.

Repulsion 2 (metal) Frequency once per minute; Effect The aspect grants all allies wearing metal armor within its aura a +1 status bonus to AC for 1 round.

Heightened (8th) Elemental Magic Cantrip: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.iYRDFxeVpJ5KIjmr]{Needle Darts}, 1st: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.2tHYKoVc5YhSewDO]{Leaden Steps}; 3rd: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Tx8OqkBFA2QlaldW]{Magnetic Acceleration}; 6th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.CB5TlGv5ZghtMifi]{Wall of Metal}, 8th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.89Hj5QuqvcwVXcqj]{Ferrous Form}

Water Aspect

This elemental is made of liquid or ice, like a brineshark or icewyrm.

Traits water

Languages Thalassic

Skills Athletics, Acrobatics

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.6UOfXUjzQQrz03Y9]{Sourced} varies (see Water Aura);

Resistances varies (see Water Aura); Weaknesses varies (see Water Aura);

Water Aura Select one of the following abilities. Choose either churning aura or freezing aura.

Churning Aura (aura 15 feet, water) Water roils around the aspect. The aspect’s Strikes deal bludgeoning damage. All non-magical fires in the area are extinguished and creatures with a swim Speed treat water in the area as if it were difficult terrain, or greater difficult terrain if the creature does not have a swim Speed. The aspect gains the Swimmer aspect ability. The aspect has a resistance to fire and a weakness to electricity and is sourced by water.

Freezing Aura (aura 15 feet, cold) The air freezes around the aspect. All non-magical liquids in the aura, such as alchemical elixirs or holy water, freeze until they spend 1 round outside the aura and are unusable. The aspect gains the cold trait and its Strikes deal cold damage. The aspect has a resistance to cold and a weakness to fire and is sourced by snow or ice.

Speed 25 feet, varies (see Water Aura)

Melee 1 primary Damage 1d8 + rank bludgeoning or cold (see Water Aura)

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains the Battering Elements activity.

Battering Elements 2 Frequency once per minute; Effect The aspect deals 1d6 damage per spell rank to all creatures within 15 feet with a basic Reflex save. The precipitation has the following effect depending on your choice for Water Aura and gains either the water trait or cold trait.

Churning Aura (water) The damage is bludgeoning and creatures that critically fail their save are pushed 10 feet away from the water elemental.

Freezing Aura (cold) The damage is cold and creatures that critically fail their save are immobilized for 1 round or until they Interact to remove the immobilized condition.

Heightened (8th) Elemental Magic Cantrip: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.IxhGEKl63R4QBvkj]{Frostbite} (cold), @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.eSL5hVT9gXrnRLtd]{Spout} (water); 1st: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.8TQiFzGf4feoHeH0]{Chilling Spray} (cold), @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.jfVCuOpzC6mUrf6f]{Hydraulic Push} (water); 3rd: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.oUDNCArkQTdhllxD]{Aqueous Orb} (water), @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.mtlyAyf30JnIvxVn]{Moonlight Ray} (cold); 6th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.9W2Qv0wXLg6tQg3y]{Scintillating Safeguard}; 8th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.C2GYCH3TtUFqPfdX]{Arctic Rift} (cold), @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.0fjz8qc9NfkmWmJZ]{Whirlpool} (water)

Wood Aspect

This elemental is composed entirely of plantlife, like a nursery crawler or painted stag.

Traits plant, wood

Languages Arboreal, Muan

Skills Nature, Stealth

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.6UOfXUjzQQrz03Y9]{Sourced} (wood objects or wooden plants)

Resistances poison; Weaknesses axe, fire

Grove Aura (aura 15 feet, plant, wood) Plantlife grows quickly around the wood aspect, teeming with life. The first time each turn a creature uses an action or activity with the plant or wood traits, it regains Hit Points equal to twice the rank of the spell that summoned the wood elemental.

Speed 25 feet

Melee 1 primary, Damage 1d8 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing

Heightened (4th) The wood elemental gains the Splinter Wood activity.

Splinter Wood 2 (plant, wood) Frequency once per minute; Effect The wood elemental causes non-magical wooden objects in a 15-foot burst within 30 feet to take 1d8 piercing damage per rank of the spell with a basic Fortitude save. Creatures adjacent to a wooden object that gained the broken condition or was destroyed by this ability also take the damage from the spell.

Heightened (8th) Elemental Magic cantrip: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.uZK2BYzPnxUBnDjr]{Tangle Vine}; 1st: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.b6AQvzs8EotmlK56]{Flourishing Flora}; 3rd: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.KsWhliKfUs3IpW3c]{Wall of Thorns}; 6th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.JbAcSLu62TU1OgNF]{Tangling Creepers}, 8th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.4MOew29Z1oCX8O28]{Moment of Renewal}

Mystic Duo.name: Mystic Duo
Mystic Duo.text:
Whether it’s their twin brother who protects them from physical harm, the royal heir who they must protect and nurture, a lifelong friend, or just an ally of convenience, mages throughout history have found themselves tied to another person. In these cases, they often form a link so strong it becomes mystic in nature. This link allows you and your companion to anticipate each other's actions, speak telepathically, share magical energy, and bolster each other's mental defenses. A duo is a partnership, and like any good partnership it is only as good as the bonded and the efforts they share to achieve the goals of both parties in the union.

Celestial Aspects.name: Celestial Aspects
Celestial Aspects.text:
All celestial aspects have the following statistics in addition to the statistics listed for their aspect.

Traits celestial, holy

Senses darkvision

Languages Empyrean

Skills Religion

Weaknesses unholy

Save Adjustments Choose a save for each modifier: –3, +1, +1

Celestial Gift Choose either the gift of flight or the gift of vitality.

Gift of Flight The aspect gains the Flier aspect ability.

Gift of Vitality (healing, vitality) The aspect is an entirely good creature. The aspect can restore 1d6 Hit Points per rank of the spell to an adjacent creature as a single action. The creature is then temporarily immune to this effect for 1 hour.

Speed 25 feet

Melee 1 primary, Damage 1d6 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing

Holy The aspect deals 1 additional spirit damage per weapon damage die to creatures with the unholy trait and its Strikes have the holy trait.

Agathion Aspect

This animal-like celestial, like a vulpinal or a procyal.

Traits agathion

Languages speak with animals but only for animals related to its Aspect of the Beast.

Skills Nature, Survival

Aspect of the Beast Select an animal type (such as feline for a silvanshee)

Save Adjustments Fort –2, Ref +1, Will +0

Melee 1 secondary (agile), Damage 1d4 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains an additional benefit from its Celestial Gift.

Gift of Flight The aspect gains either the Climber or Swimmer aspect ability depending on its choice of Aspect of the Beast (subject to GM discretion).

Gift of Vitality The aspect can deal vitality damage to an adjacent creature of the same amount it would normally restore with a basic Fortitude save.

Heightened (8th) The aspect gains one of the activities listed for an 4th-rank animal aspect as appropriate for its Aspect of the Beast (subject to GM discretion) and increases the damage die of its secondary attack by one step.

Angel Aspect

This celestial is of Nirvana, like a choral or a tabellia.

Traits angel

Skills Diplomacy, Medicine

Song of the Angels (auditory, aura 15 feet, emotion) The aspect grants all allies within 15 feet a +1 status bonus to saves against auditory and fear effects.

Ranged 1 secondary (range 60 feet), Damage 1d6 + rank piercing or 1d4 + rank sonic

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains an additional benefit from its Celestial Gift.

Gift of Flight The aspect increases its Speed by 15 feet.

Gift of Vitality The aspect can cast heal as a spell equal to half the spell’s rank, but if it does the aspect spell ends.

Heightened (8th) The aspect’s aura from Song of the Angels grants all allies a +1 status bonus to AC and saves and doubles the status bonus against auditory and fear effects.

Archon Aspect

This celestial is a Heavenly warrior of justice such as a zoaem or an aesra.

Traits archon

Skills Athletics, Intimidation

Resistances fire

Archon's Protection R Trigger An enemy damages the aspect's ally and both are within 15 feet of the aspect; Effect The ally gains resistance equal to twice the spell’s rank to the triggering damage.

Melee 1 secondary, Damage 1d4 + rank fire

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains an additional benefit from its Celestial Gift.

Gift of Flight The aspect can Fly up to half its fly Speed towards the triggering ally when it uses Archon’s Protection.

Gift of Vitality The aspect can make a melee Strike against the triggering enemy when it uses Archon’s Protection if the enemy is within range.

Heightened (8th) The aspect gains the Behold! Activity.

Behold! 2 (concentrate, emotion, fear, illusion, visual) The aspect reveals its true nature to all enemies within 30 feet. Creatures in the area must make a Will save or become frightened 1 (frightened 2 on a critical failure). Frightened creatures lose their resistance or immunity to fire damage from the aspect’s effects. Creatures are then temporarily immune to this effect for 1 minute.

Azata Aspect

This mercurial celestial hails from Elysium, like a lyrakien or a kanya.

Traits azata

Skills Diplomacy, Performance

Resistances acid, cold, electricity, or fire; Weaknesses cold iron

Freedom of the Azata (auditory, aura 15 feet, emotion) The aspect grants all allies within 15 feet a +1 status bonus to Escape checks and to saves against effects that would give it the grabbed, immobilized, or restrained conditions. The aspect treats difficult terrain as normal terrain.

Ranged 1 secondary (range 60 feet), Damage 1d4 + rank piercing

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains an additional benefit from its Celestial Gift.

Gift of Flight The aspect increases its Speed by 15 feet.

Gift of Vitality The aspect sings and inspires all within range. All allies within 30 feet gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls.

Heightened (8th) The aspect gains the Liberate action.

Liberate 1 (concentrate) The aspect loosen the bonds holding a creature back. A creature of its choice within 30 feet can a ttempt to Escape as a free action. The creature is then temporarily immune for 1 hour.

Monitor Aspects.name: Monitor Aspects
Monitor Aspects.text:
All monitor aspects have the following statistics in addition to the statistics listed for their aspect.

Traits monitor

Senses darkvision

Languages two languages from the outer planes and one common language

Skills Religion, one skill of your choice

Monitor’s Directive Choose either the directive of guidance or the directive of punishment.

Directive of Guidance The aspect can teach others its ways well. It gains the Enhanced Aid (Religion) aspect ability.

Directive of Punishment The aspect seeks to destroy those that defy it. It deals 1 additional spirit damage per weapon damage die to creatures listed in the aspect’s Punished Creatures.

Save Adjustments Choose a save for each modifier: –3,+1,+1

Speed 25 feet

Melee 1 primary, Damage 1d8 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing

Aeon Aspect

This monitor is from Axis, like an axiomite or a pleroma.

Senses envisioning (aura, divine, mental) 100 feet.

Languages envisioning

Punished Creatures demons, proteans, azata, and creatures that promote chaos (subject to GM discretion)

Perfect Averages 1 (fortune) The aspect makes a Strike. It does not roll damage and instead automatically deals the average damage. For example, rather than rolling 2d8 for damage, it takes a value of 9 instead of the roll and adds any flat damage as normal.

Heightened (4th) The aeon gains an additional benefit from its Monitor’s Directive.

Directive of Guidance Once per round, the aspect can use Aid as a free action instead of a reaction.

Directive of Punishment When the aspect uses Perfect Averages, its Strike gains the fatal trait.

Heightened (8th) The aspect gains the Fundamental Sphere action.

Fundamental Sphere 2 (concentrate, manipulate) The aspect creates a sphere with varying effects depending on its choice for Monitor’s Directive. The sphere appears within 30 feet of the aeon in a 5-foot burst and lasts for 1 minute. The aspect can spend a single action with the concentrate trait to move the sphere to another location within 30 feet of it. Essence casters have no need for an effect that replenishes a missing spell slot. Instead, a bloodrager with 0 essence who uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.XKAlLI17siAXFFyD]{Siphon Magic} feat on an enemy can use a draw cantrip to gain essence again during the encounter, even though they don’t have the essence rebirth class feature. The wizard’s @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.classfeatures.au0lwQ1nAcNQwcGh]{arcane bond} feature grants you a prepared spell or spells instead of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.v82XtjAVN4ffgVVR]{Drain Bonded Item}; you gain an additional spell prepared of any rank the bonded item could have provided a spell slot (one of up to your highest rank for most wizards, or one of each rank for wizards of the school of unified magic theory).

Freeze Time

Some spells like freeze time allow you to take several turns in a row. In these situations, you normally can’t gain or use essence, so you need to cast cantrips and focus spells. This makes those spells less useful unless you have focus spells or items you’d like to use during the frozen time. You can instead use this essence casting version of freeze time, replacing the normal effects of the spell.

You temporarily stop time for everything but yourself, allowing you to use several actions in what appears to others to be no time at all. Immediately after casting freeze time, you can use up to 9 actions in 3 sets of up to 3 actions each. While time is frozen, your essence draw and essence pool are 1 lower than normal, and you can’t use essence rebirth; if you would complete an essence cycle, you experience an essence leak instead, and at the end of the frozen time, you immediately experience an essence leak and return to 0 essence. After each set of actions, 1 round passes, but for only you, effects specifically targeting or affecting you, and effects that you create during the stoppage. All other creatures and objects are invulnerable to your attacks, and you can't target or affect them with anything. Once you have finished your actions, time begins to flow again for the rest of the world. If you created an effect with a duration that extends beyond freeze time's duration, such as wall of fire, it immediately affects others again, but it doesn't have any of the effects that happen only when you first Cast the Spell.

Staves empowered by essence prepared casters function as if they were staves for spontaneous casters (1 charge gains you access to the spells on the staves list as if you had them prepared).

You can instead use this essence casting version of the class feat Quickened Spell, replacing the normal effects of the feat (retaining all other aspects of the feat such as frequency):

“If your next action is to cast an essence spell of a rank less than or equal to your essence draw, reduce the number of actions to cast it by 1 (minimum 1 action). It doesn't cause an essence leak or increase your current essence, and you can cast another essence spell this turn.”

You can choose to gain 2 fewer spells prepared, both of which must be of the same rank, to grant a number of charges to your staff equal to the rank of the chosen spells during your daily preparations instead of the ability to expend a spell slot to gain charges.

If you Cast a Spell that would increase your essence and take 2 rounds to cast, such as horizon thunder sphere, you increase your essence by 1 each round you Cast the Spell.

Prerequisites You are a spellcaster that gains @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.items.nWrMVX6rsQanqjlj]{Unstable Draw} as a class feature

Gaining Essence in Encounters

When you’re in a combat encounter (or rarely in another dire and stressful situation, as determined by your GM), the magical essence you channel for your spell’s tradition gathers in your body, mind, lifeforce, and spirit. As you chain your magic, your essence grows, until you reach your apex. If you have the essence rebirth class feature, you can then begin again.

When you start an encounter, you normally have 0 essence, but you can use a draw cantrip to increase your essence up to your essence draw value. If you have more than 0 essence, once per turn you may cast an essence spell with a rank up to the amount of essence you have. After casting an essence spell in this way, if you used at least 2 actions for your Cast a Spell activity, you increase your essence by 1, otherwise you cause an essence leak. If an effect would normally expend a spell slot without you having to Cast the Spell, such as the Channeling Block cleric feat, you expend your essence instead and cause an essence leak.

If gaining essence would put you above your essence pool (normally equal to the highest rank spell prepared or in your repertoire, not counting 10th-rank spells, see below), if you’re a normal spellcaster, you complete an essence cycle and your essence returns to 0. Unless you have the essence rebirth class feature, you can’t gain essence again until the next time you’re in a different encounter, or dire and stressful situation.

Essence Leaks

When you cause an essence leak, you reduce your current essence to 0 immediately after you Cast the Spell that caused the essence leak and you fail to complete an essence cycle and you cannot draw essence again unless you have the essence rebirth class feature.

Durations and Temporary Immunity

All essence spells end as soon as the encounter ends. Since you can’t gather essence round by round outside of an encounter, you can instead cast any spell you’ve prepared or in your repertoire with an incantation or a long incantation.

All of your essence spells that counteract effects, reduce or remove conditions or afflictions, and so on grant temporary immunity to their target for 1 day after you cast them. This temporary immunity only applies to the same spell cast by you.

Classes With Unusual Numbers of Slots

Some classes have more or fewer slots than the baseline amount that classes like bards, clerics, or druids have, where they gain up to 3 slots per rank, and these classes are treated differently in essence casting as well.

Classes that grant up to 4 slots per rank like sorcerer and wizard (but not classes like animist that have a unique structure that adds up to 4 slots) gain an added benefit starting at 3rd level: for every rank aside from their maximum rank, they get 5 spell slots or spells in their repertoire instead of 4. So at 3rd level, they would have 5 1st-rank spells and 3 2nd-rank spells. Universalist wizards gain the same benefit because of the way their bonded item grants them additional spell slots, bringing them up to 4 slots in practice (see page 71 for more information on bonded items).

Psychics, which grant up to 2 slots per rank, instead gain a restriction: They can’t use the unstable draw feature normally gained at 5th level, and the first time they cast an essence spell during an encounter, they automatically experience an essence leak. They can’t use any other effect that would grant them a greater benefit in exchange for a leak on this guaranteed leak.

Animists work a little differently than other spellcasters and so they have their own rules. An animist only gains as many apparition spells of each rank as they have slots for apparition spells of that rank, which is typically 1 for their top 2 ranks and 2 for the rest. They choose from among the spells granted by all their apparitions. Only 1 apparition spell at each rank is a signature spell, and they can choose which of the ones they picked to be the signature spell at each rank. As stated above, animists don't gain a 5th spell slot at their lower ranks like sorcerers or wizards do. Instead, they effectively gain the benefits of prepared casting for half their spell slots while still having as many signature spells as a spontaneous spellcaster.

Construct Aspects.name: Construct Aspects
Construct Aspects.text:
All construct aspects have the following statistics in addition to the statistics listed for their aspect.

Traits construct, mindless

Senses darkvision

Languages Common; (can’t speak)

Skills Athletics, Crafting

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.6UOfXUjzQQrz03Y9]{Sourced} (statue or unworn suit of heavy armor)

Save Adjustments Fort +2, Ref –3, Will –1

Immunities bleed, death effects, disease, doomed, drained, fatigued, fear, healing, mental, nonlethal attacks, paralyzed, poison, sickened, spirit, unconscious, vitality, void

Speed 20 feet

Animated Aspect

This construct is a piece of craft given life, like animated armor or an animated colossus.

Construct Armor The aspect has Hardness equal to twice the rank of the spell. Once the construct is reduced to fewer than half its Hit Points, or immediately upon being damaged by a critical hit, its constructed armor breaks, it loses its Hardness and takes a –2 status penalty to AC and all of its saves for the duration of the spell.

Melee 1 primary, Damage 1d8 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains a +1 status bonus to Athletics checks to Grapple. It gains the Capture action.

Capture 1 Requirements The aspect has a creature at least one size smaller than it restrained by its Grapple; Effect The creature is restrained until it Escapes and the aspect can use the limb it used for the Grapple. It can only have a single creature occupied in this way at a time.

Heightened (8th) The aspect gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.UNah0bxXxkcZjxO3]{Trample} aspect ability.

Clockwork Aspect

This construct is composed of fine, intricate mechanisms, like a clockwork soldier or clockwork serpent.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.6UOfXUjzQQrz03Y9]{Sourced} (clockwork parts)

Resistances physical; Weaknesses electricity

Ranged 1 primary (range 60 feet, reload 1), Damage 1d6 + rank bludgeoning

Wind-Up Key The aspect has a key in its back which can be wound up to increase the power of the aspect. The key can be wound with a single Interact action, which reloads its primary attack, and gives it a +10-foot status bonus to its Speed for 1 round.

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains the Clockwork Blast activity.

Clockwork Blast 1 Requirements The aspect’s primary attack is loaded; Effect All creatures within a 30-foot cone take twice the damage of its primary Strike with a basic Reflex save. It cannot use Clockwork Blast again until it has had its key wound three times.

Heightened (8th) The aspect gains the Overclock free action.

Overclock � Requirements A creature wound its key at least once since the aspect’s last turn; Effect The aspect is quickened for a number of rounds equal to the number of times its key was turned. The aspect can use the extra action each round for only Strike and Stride actions.

Guardian Aspect

This construct was designed to protect, like an iron warden or a golem.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.6UOfXUjzQQrz03Y9]{Sourced} (statue or unworn suit of heavy armor)

Resistances physical

Interposing Presence Allies adjacent to the aspect gain lesser cover

Melee 1 primary, Damage 1d4 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains the Punish Instigators reaction.

Punish Instigators 1 Trigger A creature Strikes an ally adjacent to the aspect with standard cover; Effect The aspect Strikes the creature. If the aspect’s Strike is a critical hit, the creature is shoved 10 feet away from the construct, potentially disrupting the Strike.

Heightened (8th) Allies adjacent to the aspect gain standard cover instead of lesser cover. On Reflex saves to avoid a damaging effect, such as a fireball, the aspect uses its Fortitude modifier instead of its Reflex modifier.

Unnatural Aspect

This unsettling construct is made of organic parts, such as a scarecrow, necrophidus or fleshwarp.

Skills Intimidation

Intimidating Glare The aspect gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.xQMz6eDgX75WX2ce]{Intimidating Glare} skill feat.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.6UOfXUjzQQrz03Y9]{Sourced} (corpse or organic material)

Living Parts The aspect’s body is made of tissue, such as flesh, bone or straw. It is not immune to bleed, disease, drained, mental, nonlethal, poison, sickened, vitality, or void, and is healed for half the normal amount by healing effects.

Melee 1 primary, Damage 1d6 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing Melee 1 secondary (agile), Damage 1d4 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing

Heightened (4th) The aspect deals 1 additional damage per weapon damage die to creatures that are frightened, and it gains the Frightening Features ability.

Frightening Features (aura 15-feet, emotion, fear, mental, visual) The aspect’s appearance is distressing to many. The first time a creature enters the aura, it must make a Will save or become frightened 1 (frightened 2 on a critical failure). Regardless of the result, the creature is then temporarily immune for 1 minute.

Heightened (8th) The aspect is healed normally by healing effects The area for Frightening Features is increased to 30 feet, and the additional damage it deals to frightened creatures is doubled.

Dragon Aspects.name: Dragon Aspects
Dragon Aspects.text:
All dragon aspects have the following statistics in addition to the statistics listed for their aspect.

Traits dragon

Senses darkvision

Languages Draconic

Skills one skill determined by Magic of the Dragon

Magic of the Dragon The aspect gains a trait associated with your magical tradition and you can only choose dragon aspects with traits that correspond to your tradition. Your aspect adds the skill associated with its tradition to its list of skills.

Save Adjustments Fort +1, Ref –3, Will +1

Resistances varies (see Draconic Damage)

Draconic Damage Choose one of the damage types listed for your dragon aspect.: acid, cold, electricity, fire, mental, poison, spirit, sonic, vitality, or void. The dragon has resistance to its draconic damage type.

Speed 25 feet

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.rU0OMGjiOo6xc7BR]{Flier} The aspect has the Flier aspect ability.

Melee 1 primary, Damage 1d8 + rank piercing

Melee 1 secondary (agile or reach), Damage 1d4 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing

Breath Weapon 2 (magical) Frequency once per minute; Effect The dragon can unleash a blast of draconic breath, dealing 1d6 damage per spell rank to all creatures within a 15- foot cone or a 30-foot line with basic Reflex save. The damage type is determined by your choice of draconic damage.

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains immunity to its draconic damage type instead of resistance. The dragon’s breath weapon damage doubles and the area increases to a 30-foot cone or a 60-foot line, depending on your choice of area.

Heightened (8th) When the aspect critically succeeds at a Strike or it successfully Strikes a creature twice in the same turn, it regains the use of its breath weapon again. The aspect gains the Draconic Frenzy activity.

Draconic Frenzy 2 The aspect makes two primary Strikes and one secondary Strike in any order.

Lorekeeper Aspect

A lorekeeper is a dragon with a wealth of strange knowledge, such as a mirage or conspirator dragon.

Skills Diplomacy or Society, Secrets Lore

Magic of the Dragon arcane or occult

Spellcasting Dragon The aspect can cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.izcxFQFwf3woCnFs]{Guidance} as an innate cantrip of your tradition.

Knower of Secrets The aspect’s knowledge of secrets is vast. It gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.zSlBwwLCDeSQBSoi]{Enhanced Aid (Secrets Lore)} aspect ability.

Planarist Aspect

This dragon is empowered by otherworldly forces, like diabolic dragons or brine dragons.

Skills Intimidation, Planar Lore

Magic of the Dragon divine or primal

Empowered Striker Choose fire, physical, or spirit. The aspect deals 1 additional damage per weapon damage die of the chosen type on its primary Strikes or the same damage as the Strike if you chose physical.

Rampager Aspect

This dragon values brute force and power, like a barrage or a horned dragon.

Skills Intimidation, Disaster Lore

Magic of the Dragon arcane or primal

Razing Rampage 3 The aspect Strides twice and makes two Strikes at any point of its turn.

Spiritualist Aspect

This dragon is empowered by ethereal energies, like omen dragons or umbral dragons.

Skills Deception, Spirit Lore

Magic of the Dragon divine or occult

Mend the Spirit R Frequency once per minute; Trigger The aspect is hit by a Strike; Effect The aspect either alters fate or alters into a spirit form to avoid the Strike. The aspect gains physical resistance against the triggering Strike equal to twice the rank of the spell.

Devastator of the Spirit The aspect’s Strikes affect incorporeal creatures with the effects of a ghost touch property rune.

Pest Aspect.name: Pest Aspect
Pest Aspect.text:
The pest aspect is a small critter or vermin, like a rat, cat or insect.

Traits animal

Senses low-light vision, scent (imprecise) 30 feet

Skills Athletics, Acrobatics, Stealth

Save Adjustments Fort –2, Ref +1, Will +0

Weaknesses physical

Speed 20 feet

Just a Pest A pest aspect cannot make Strikes and its maximum size is always Tiny.

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains your choice of the Climber, Flier, or Swimmer aspect abilities.

Heightened (8th) The aspect gains two skills of your choice.

Undead Aspects.name: Undead Aspects
Undead Aspects.text:
All undead aspects have the following statistics in addition to the statistics listed for their aspect.

Traits undead

Senses darkvision

Languages Necril

Skills see text (Undead Mind)

Sourced (corpse or grave) The spell gains the unholy trait.

Save Adjustments Choose a save for each modifier: –2,+0,+1 or –3,+1,+1 or –3,+0,+2

Void Healing The aspect has void healing.

Undead Immunities death effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, precision, unconscious

Undead Mind Choose either mindless or minded.
Mindless The aspect gains the mindless trait and a weakness to vitality damage. It is immune to mental effects and it cannot speak or use actions with the concentrate trait. The aspect adds 1 skill of its choice to its aspect.
Minded The aspect adds 3 skills of its choice to its aspect, two of which must share the same attribute modifier.

Speed 25 feet

Corpse Aspect

This undead is a corpse, like a zombie, ghoul, or a wight.

Melee 1 primary, Damage 1d8 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing or Melee 1 primary (agile), Damage 1d6 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing

Mass of Flesh Increase the number of Hit Points per rank of the spell for the aspect by 1.

Heightened (4th) Choose between Grapple or Shove. It gains the Grasp of the Dead reaction.

Grasp of the Dead R Trigger The aspect critically hits with its primary Strike; Effect The aspect attempts the chosen Athletics maneuver against the target of the Strike. This attack counts toward its multiple attack penalty, but the maneuver is made at the same multiple attack penalty as the triggering Strike.

Heightened (8th) The aspect gains the Gruesome Display ability.

Gruesome Display (visual) When the aspect is critically hit by a Strike, enemies within a 30-foot emanation must attempt a Fortitude save or become sickened 1 (sickened 2 on a critical failure). Regardless of the result, the enemy is then immune for 1 minute.

ETERNAL Aspect

This undead is a horror that retains its soul, like a vampire, mummy, or lich.

Melee 1 primary, Damage 1d8 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing or Ranged 1 primary (range of 30 feet), Damage 1d6 + rank void

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains the Drain Essence reaction.

Drain Essence R Trigger The aspect dealt damage with a Strike; Effect The aspect drains a creature, absorbing its essence and regains Hit Points equal to half the damage of the triggering Strike.

Heightened (8th) The aspect gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.u098thIGDlrHC8G8]{Caster} aspect ability. Cantrip: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.mAMEt4FFbdqoRnkN]{Void Warp}, 1st: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.vLA0q0WOK2YPuJs6]{Charm} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.wdA52JJnsuQWeyqz]{Harm}, 2nd: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.JhRuR7Jj3ViShpq7]{Ghoulish Cravings}, 3rd: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.IihxWhRfpsBgQ5jS]{Enthrall}, 4th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.qwlh6aDgi86U3Q7H]{Suggestion}, 5th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.GaRQlC9Yw1BGKHfN]{Wave of Despair}, 6th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.OsOhx3TGIZ7AhD0P]{Dominate}, 7th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Z9OrRXKgAPv6Hn5l]{Execute}, 8th: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.HEuvZAjD1q0J8Y5i]{Unholy Army}

iNCORPOREAL Aspect

This undead is a terrifying, ethereal thing, like a ghost, poltergeist or shadow.

Traits incorporeal

Anchored Incorporeality (you)

Speed 10 feet, hover 25 feet

Flier The aspect gains the Flier aspect ability.

Melee 1 primary, Damage 1d6 + rank void or Ranged 1 primary (range 30 feet), Damage 1d4 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing

Fade 1 The aspect becomes invisible until it performs a hostile action. It cannot use Fade again for [[/r 1d4]] rounds after using a hostile action.

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains a fly Speed of 30 feet and loses anchored incorporeality.

Heightened (8th) The aspect gains the Terrifying Shriek activity.

Terrifying Shriek 2 (auditory, emotion, fear, mental) Frequency once per minute; Effect The aspect emits a bloodcurdling scream or a mortifying display, dealing 2d6 mental damage per spell rank to all creatures within a 15-foot emanation with a basic WIll save. Creatures that critically fail their save are also frightened 2.

sLOUGH Aspect

This undead is the husk of a creature, like a skeleton, beetle carapace, or hollow serpent.

Resistances piercing and slashing; Weaknesses bludgeoning

Collapse 1 Trigger The aspect is critically hit by a Strike; Effect The aspect collapses into pieces and the triggering Strike is treated as a normal success. The aspect can re-form in a standing position as an action, but until it does, it is immobilized and off-guard.

Melee 1 primary, Damage 1d8 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing

Melee 1 primary (agile), Damage 1d6 + rank bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing

Heightened (4th) The aspect gains a burrow Speed of 15 feet.

Heightened (8th) The aspect no longer has a weakness to bludgeoning damage.

Aspect Casting.name: Aspect Casting
Aspect Casting.text: Aspect casting is to form an aspect of your design from the fabrics of magic itself. Aspect casters have learned to manifest creatures from these designs, either as an extension of their mind or spirit, or by molding their own physical form. Aspect magic is much like other magic, except they are formed at the time of casting in the image of their makings desires, their power and abilities derived from the very fabric of the wielder’s magic instead of as a means to adapt creatures that already exist. In this method of shape changing and summoning, that which is created is truly an extension of the wielder instead of a mere adaptation or representative from another plane.

Archmage.name: Archmage
Archmage.text:
uncommon

The archmage is the pinnacle of all that most wizards seek to achieve when they first begin to uncover the secrets of magic. Sadly for most, a true archmage must wield energies far beyond those most spellcasters are capable of obtaining. Fortunately for you, those energies are already within your grasp.

Your careful and measured blending of mythic power with eldritch energies allows you to unleash potent magic similar to the embodiments of mythic magic known as wildspells, but unlike those unbound cascades of magical energy, you have built barriers and limits around your magic that keep it from overwhelming your mortal constraints. You lack the burning eyes and swirling magical aura that makes a wildspell plain to see, though any spellcaster who spends much time in your presence is likely to sense hints of the tightly constrained power within you. Magic hangs like a heavy shroud around you, invisible to the eye but near-stifling in the weight of its immensity.

On Golarion and its neighboring planet of Akiton, there is no archmage better known than Old-Mage Jatembe (meddling male human halcyon speaker), whose actions have protected Golarion’s people and magical traditions for centuries.

Merlin (cunning male human wizard) is perhaps the most famous archmage across the greater span of all existence, with a name known across multiple worlds and planes. Famed for his penchant for meddling and habit of entrusting world-changing artifacts to young knights, this wizard above wizards is a paragon that many would-be archmages strive to emulate.

Stardust (adventurous male ancestry-unknown space traveler) is an archmage who used his magic to significantly modify his own body before using his spells to travel the farthest reaches of space and time. Stardust’s reputation on the various planets he’s visited is mixed at best, due to his habit of using reality-bending spells to punish criminals when the lasting effects of the spell seem wildly disproportionate to the offense that elicited them.

Whatever your story and reputation are now, only time will tell if you are truly worthy to claim the mantle of archmage. The seeds of power are within your grasp. The path is open before you. Craft your spells, wield the magic of the immortals, and bend reality itself to your whim. Only then will you be worthy of the title of archmage!

Essence Casting.name: Essence Casting
Essence Casting.text:
Essence Casters vs Vancian Casters

Essence casting allows a spellcaster to cast more spells from some of their best ranks in a day than normal, especially in a day with a large number of encounters. While it might be most dramatic at lower levels when spells are scarce for Vancian spellcasters, this pattern remains the same even at higher levels.

However, it comes at a significant cost: Vancian spellcasters can place powerful buffs and environmental control effects before the fight, repeat recovery spells as long as they have slots to spend, and unleash all their best spells back to back in a crisis. For an example at higher levels, an essence casting 18th-level wizard could cast a 7th-, 8th-, and 9th-rank spell every single encounter of the day, and if the encounter is tougher than expected and stretches on to 7 rounds, they could even cast 2 of each of those ranks and a cantrip. However, if the Vancian wizard goes in completely fresh to that tough encounter, they could cast five 9th-rank spells and two 8th-rank spells. And supposing the tough fight is 5 rounds long instead, the essence wizard is potentially using two cantrips and one each of 7th-, 8th-, and 9th-rank while the Vancian wizard can just unload a 9th-rank spell every single round.

As a result, while they don’t have the same potential to unload all at once, essence casters will usually be much more consistent across a longer adventuring day, and hopefully more fun to play in those easier encounters since you can cast some of your more impactful spells without feeling like you’re leaving yourself vulnerable in case a hard fight comes later in the day!

Magic is formed of four essences: life, matter, mind, and spirit. When two of the four essences of magic are woven together, they form the magical traditions of arcane, divine, occult, and primal magic. While some spellcasters try to conceptualize these essences in discrete “slots” to be used once and faded away into the ether, there are others who focus on the way these essences coalesce into usable form in order to follow the natural cycle of magic, rather than the casting approach these essence casters see as “brute force.” Different cultures have their own name for this phenomenon, but all agree on the fundamentals. The structure of the coalesced essence depends on whether it is physical or spiritual: material essence is physical and travels through a spellcaster’s body almost like blood travels through veins and arteries, while spiritual essence likewise travels through a spellcaster’s soul. Similarly, the way the coalesced essence is energized and moves depends on whether the essence is mental or vital: mental essence responds best to conscious thought and the workings of the mind, while vital essence reacts reflexively based on instinct or faith, like how sometimes people can display abnormal strength in a crisis. Arcane essence is material and mental, divine essence is spiritual and vital, occult essence is spiritual and mental, and primal essence is material and vital.

What is Essence Casting?

Essence casting is an all-day spellcasting system that allows your character to gather essence throughout the battle to cast more powerful spells, rather than limiting spells based on daily spell slots. Full spellcasters can complete essence cycles or cause essence leaks to develop one of several possible strategies, potentially choosing between them on the fly. Essence casting can replace slot-based spellcasting in your game, but if not everyone in your group wants to use essence casting, you could make essence casting into a class archetype instead which grants essence casting to those who take it.

Is Essence Casting For You?

If you always felt uncomfortable with the daily preparation of spells or especially with the need to either stockpile resources and use them sparingly or else blow through them and demand a rest while the rest of the characters are still ready to continue, essence casting is the perfect fit for you. It’s also especially strong in campaigns with a large number of encounters each day, whether they are easier encounters (in which case you’ll make a much bigger impact in every encounter compared to holding back your slots) or harder encounters (in which case you can handle more of them before you’re running on fumes).

However, if you love Vancian casting or your campaigns usually have one or two big fights per day where everyone “novas,” leading with their most powerful abilities at once, essence casting might not be for you. Then again, even when essence casting isn’t as powerful as traditional spellcasting, you might find that it’s more fun for you. Especially if there’s always a specter of another encounter or a night ambush causing you to hold back. Essence casting also isn’t for spellcasters who like to put up a lot of long-lasting effects out of combat, as it’s highly focused on the spells you cast during combat.

For an adventuring day of roughly three to six encounters with a significant enough challenge that spellcasters would want to use their main spells instead of relying on focus spells or cantrips, you should find that the two systems each have strengths and weaknesses (with essence casting getting stronger as you rise in the number of encounters): you can often pull off more of your best spells more confidently with essence casting, but you can cast them exactly when you want them during a given fight with Vancian casting, as long as you have slots left to do so.

Example of Play

Basic Tactics

While essence casting isn’t inherently more complicated than managing spell slots, the complexity lies in a different place, so it’s likely to seem that way at first if you’re used to traditional spellcasting systems. To help you get started, here’s three of the most basic tactics available to full spellcasters starting from 3rd level. Essence cycles tend to be the default for most spellcasters while one long chain is the default for bounded spellcasters, and essence leaks are a little more advanced.

Essence Cycle: This is the most basic strategy for a full spellcaster: you simply continue casting essence spells and building up benefits from essence cycles as long as the encounter continues.

One Long Chain: With this strategy, you stretch out a single chain of spells in an attempt to last the whole encounter. This strategy is easiest for bounded spellcasters like magus or summoner who have plenty of other things they can do with their turns to extend their chain, and who can’t essence cycle even if they wanted to, but it’s also relatively easy for classes with strong 2-action focus spells or other options for their actions than essence spells.

Essence Leak: This is a more advanced strategy than the others for a full spellcaster; you intentionally break your essence cycles early in order to use 1- action or reaction spells with high frequency, with the cost being that you’ll usually need to be casting draw cantrips on your turn. This strategy works best when coordinating with your team and might not be beneficial for all groups compared to a more active essence cycle. For the simplest example of a low-level essence leak strategy, suppose your group skirmished with multiple foes while you were using lose the path turn after turn to shave off multiple actions from different enemies each turn.

Vasvali, a 5th-level witch, and Ruka, a 5th-level wizard, are travelling alongside some companions. Both casters use essence magic, meaning they don’t use spell slots, and can cast magic as often as they like without running out. Ruka is a more traditional caster who is content following a regular essence cycle; Vasvali, however, is more experimental in her magic, and can take tactical risks and gambles others might not.

At some point in their journey, they are set upon by a group of goblin bandits. As combat begins, both Vasvali and Ruka begin drawing power for free. (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.items.cYHvzy96aWk5n8yC]{Initial Draw}). They both begin with an essence level of 1, meaning they can only cast 1st-rank spells or cantrips. If they were any more unpracticed, they would begin with an essence level of 0, and would need to rely on a cantrip to begin drawing power (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.items.jNOZkBE8sd1UhH8o]{Draw Cantrips}).

As combat starts, the two casters begin casting spells; Ruka unleashes a blast of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.y6rAdMK6EFlV6U0t]{Breathe Fire} and Strides away from the goblins. Vasvali soddens the earth with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.yAiSNmz39qXOIlco]{Mud Pit}. As both are casting spells which have two or three actions, their powers grow; their essence level increases to 2 (@UUID[.ILOvQomWxAWRXHzk#gaining-essence-in-encounters]{Gaining Essence in Encounters}).

On the second round of combat, the two have even greater magic available to them. They can cast spells of a rank equal to or lower than their current essence level. Ruka casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.9XHmC2JgTUIQ1CCm]{Mist} to provide some cover from nearby archers. Vasvali intends to uses her focus spell, @UUID[Compendium.witches-remaster.witches-remaster-focus-spells.YFusnK3S1rkhfy55]{Holding Glyph} (Witches+) to dispatch a particularly nasty bandit. Focus Spells don’t increase your essence level; however, Vasvali is not content with staying at an essence level of 2 this round. As such, she starts by using her third action to use the Essence Conduit action. This allows her to channel essence through her focus spell. When she uses holding glyph, her power grows as if she had cast an essence spell (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.misc.GMpbfdVHBUaiIwSy]{Essence Conduit}). As before, their essence level grows, now reaching 3–the highest rank they can currently cast (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.items.0KTqyVRXp6ylg39q]{Essence Pool}).

The third round provides a complication. Vasvali is wounded by a terrible strike from a goblin.

Distressed by Vasvali’s injury, Ruka runs to her aid, and casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.9AAkVUCwF6WVNNY2]{Lightning Bolt} to fry some nearby goblins. Ruka cannot form her magic into 4th-rank spells yet, and yet she has pushed beyond 3rd-rank. Ruka brings her power to an apex, and activates a cycle terminus. Focusing on her control of the essence of mind, she uses the Terminus of Insight, allowing the knowledge of the world to enter her unbidden. Her essence level drops to 0, and she can continue casting spells next turn, repeating the cycle (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.items.OGeHSfEa8N58Sp8z]{Cycle Terminus}).

Instead of casting @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.sxQZ6yqTn0czJxVd]{Fireball}, Vasvali’s wound forces her to recover, and she casts a 1-action @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal} on herself. This restores 12 HP to herself. Healing magic is difficult to manipulate too often as it interacts directly with the life essence all creatures are made of. Vasvali can heal a maximum number of hit points equal to her highest healing spell’s rank times twelve–in this case, 36. She recovers the 12 HP, so she can now only heal 24 healing for the rest of the encounter–she has to be careful how she spends it (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.items.odAsOR95Cjuwqixk]{Life Essence Reservoir}). To make matters worse, by casting a 1-action spell, Vasvali has thrown her rhythm off; she experiences an essence leak as she tries to force her magic to work quicker than it should. This means all of Vasvali’s built up essences have drained, and her essence level is reset to 0. A fair price for surviving another day, she reasons.

Only a few goblins remain now. As Ruka casts daze, she gathers some essence; her essence level is back to 1. Right before the spell was cast, she was given a free @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} by her @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.items.iHEG6M3sZEkJRedO]{Terminus of Insight} with a +2 circumstance bonus. Had the information revealed these goblins had a particular weakness or had a bad save, she would have been allowed to change the spell; satisfied with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.4gBIw4IDrSfFHik4]{Daze}, though, she casts anyway. Vasvali is a little more impatient, however; she estimates she has the perfect spell to end the fight at 2nd-rank, and doesn’t want to wait until she has drawn enough power. Forcing her way through magic again, she casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.thAHF1zxNplLCJPO]{Caustic Blast}, but rather than draw in power carefully, she performs an unstable draw. She gains 2 essence levels rather than 1, but it’s likely this will lead to another essence leak afterwards (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-magic.items.nWrMVX6rsQanqjlj]{Unstable Draw}).

Ruka casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.0uRpypf1Hi7ahvTl]{Shattering Gem} on the goblins, gaining another free Recall Knowledge. Vasvali then uses final sacrifice on her loathesome familiar, Mandukhees. The explosion defeats the last of the goblins–and in good time–as her unstable draw before did cause another essence leak, bringing her back to 0 again while Ruka had risen to 3. If Ruka had reached a cycle a second time, her Terminus of Insight would have grown even more powerful. She’s grateful that it didn’t go on any longer, though.

As combat ends, the party rests. Vasvali begins to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.OSefkMgojBLqmRDh]{Refocus} in order to get her focus points back. While she’s doing so, she automatically restores one third of her Life Essence Resevoir; 12, the same amount as she healed earlier. Ruka casts a spell outside of combat, performing an incantation. She casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.VDudQ4x2ozosAbTb]{Invisibility}; rather than being instantaneous like it might be in the heat of combat, it takes about 20 seconds to cast here. She scouts the area nearby to ensure there are no goblins before returning. When she does so, she needs to Refocus as well; if she doesn’t, the next time she enters combat, she won’t be able to draw power at all. If she had any focus points, she’d recover these at the same time. At level seven, she’ll simply have a lower draw power than normal if she entered combat without Refocusing, but for now, she needs to be careful.

Once everyone is ready, the party continues on their adventure–all without expending daily resources–fully capable for any sort of fight the day may bring them!

Aspect Forms.name: Aspect Forms
Aspect Forms.text:
Untamed Form and Form Feats

The following feats replace references to battle form spells with the corresponding aspect battle form spell. The feat grants any effects it would gain for battle forms to the corresponding spells and the specified aspects (if any).

Untamed Form: pest shift and animal shift (instead of pest form and animal form respectively)

Ferocious Shape: animal shift (instead of animal form; mount or predator aspect only)

Insect Shape: animal shift (instead of animal form; aerial or predator aspect only)

Elemental Shape: elemental shift (instead of elemental form)

Monstrosity Shape: thurse shift (instead of monstrosity form)

Plant Shape: plant shift (instead of plant form)

Reactive Transformation: animal shift (instead of aerial form; aerial aspect only)

Soaring Shape: animal shift (instead of animal form; aerial aspect only)

Darkened Forest Form: pest shift, animal shift, elemental shift (instead of pest form, animal form, and elemental form respectively)

Dragon Shape: dragon shift (instead of dragon form)

Changing into imposing creatures in battle is a staple of powerful spellcasters, but battle forms requiring bespoke values for their statistics can render these spells with awkward progressions. Aspect Forms are an alternate battle form system in which players become creatures based on specific templates called aspects, allowing forms to adapt with the spellcaster themselves instead of the rank of their spells.

When you cast an aspect spell with the polymorph trait that grants a battle form, you choose an aspect to become that is listed in the spell, gaining all of the effects appropriate for that aspect as defined in the polymorph trait for the aspect spell. The rank of the aspect battle form spell determines the effects and granted benefits of the spell. You can Dismiss an aspect battle form spell.

If your aspect makes you a Large creature, you have 10 feet of reach, if your aspect makes you a Huge creature, you have 15 feet of reach, and if your aspect makes you a Gargantuan creature you have 20 feet of reach. If you choose a size category one size category smaller than the spells maximum, you increase your land Speed by 10 feet, by 20 feet if you choose a size category two size categories smaller, or by 30 feet if you choose a size category three size categories smaller. A battle form aspect of Tiny size always has a reach of 0 feet.

All aspect battle forms gain the following effects when heightened. If an aspect has a heightened effect, it gains those effects in addition to the effects of its previous heightened entries.

Heightened (3rd) The aspect’s Strikes deal 2 weapon damage dice and increase the temporary Hit Points per rank by 1. You can be up to Large in size.

Heightened (7th) The aspect’s Strikes deal 3 weapon damage dice and increase the temporary Hit Points per rank by 2. You can be up to Huge in size.

Heightened (10th) The aspect’s Strikes deal 4 weapon damage dice and increase the temporary Hit Points per rank by 4. You can be up to Gargantuan in size.

Aspect Traits: Polymorph Trait

These effects transform the target into a new form. A target can't be under the effect of more than one polymorph effect at a time. If it comes under the effect of a second polymorph effect, the second polymorph effect attempts to counteract the first. If it succeeds, it takes effect, and if it fails, the spell has no effect on that target. Any Strikes specifically granted by a polymorph effect are magical. Unless otherwise stated, polymorph spells don't allow the target to take on the appearance of a specific individual creature, but rather just a generic creature of a general type or ancestry.

If you take on a battle form with a polymorph spell, your battle form has an AC and spell or ability DCs equal to your spell DC, and it uses your spell attack modifier for its attack rolls. The only Strikes you can make while in an aspect battle form are the Strikes granted to you by your form. You can choose to use your unarmed attack modifier for your attack rolls instead of your spell attack modifier. You are trained in the skills listed in the aspect chosen for your battle form, using either your skill modifier or your spell attack modifier for checks with that skill (whichever is higher). You modify your saves based on your chosen aspect and you gain temporary Hit Points equal to twice the rank of the spell. If the aspect you selected would increase its Hit Points, such as an animal aspect, you increase your temporary Hit Points by the same amount. You gain the abilities and senses listed for your aspect based on the rank of the battle form spell unless otherwise noted in the spell. You do not gain languages associated with the aspect but can speak and understand languages you know normally unless the aspect can’t speak. You cannot Cast a Spell while in an aspect battle form unless the aspect you select lists spells in its entry or would gain spells from an ability (such as the Caster aspect ability).

You take a cumulative –1 penalty to all your DCs and checks while in your battle form for every rank below half your level rounded up of the spell that summoned it. For instance, if you were 11th level and you cast a 4th-rank animal form spell, you would take a –2 penalty to your AC, saves, DCs, and all checks while within the battle form spell since it is 2 ranks below 6 (half your level rounded up).

If you take on a battle form with a polymorph spell, the special statistics can be adjusted only by circumstance bonuses, status bonuses, and penalties. Unless otherwise noted, the battle form prevents you from casting spells, speaking, and using most manipulate actions that require hands. (If there's doubt about whether you can use an action, the GM decides.) Your gear is absorbed into you; the constant abilities of your gear still function, but you can't activate any items. If a polymorph effect causes you to increase in size, you must have space to expand into or the effect is disrupted.
